REASONING:

Step 1 - Frame the project
- Objective: To improve the quality of tourism infrastructure and services, the conditions of natural and cultural heritage sites, and to increase sustainable tourism activity in the Arequipa-Colca corridor.
- Scope/Components:
  - Component 1: Improve the quality of selected tourism attractions and services (US$51.17M) - upgraded public tourism services, site interventions, restoration of 10 historic churches/temples, capacity building.
  - Component 2: Upgrade roads and investment in water, sanitation and health facilities (US$37.06M) - tertiary road network (vecinal) and local street revamping (AR-683, Maca-Lari, San Juan de Tarucani AR-759, Yura AR-711, Pinchollo AR-109, Sibayo and Yanque streets), water/sanitation (San Juan de Tarucani, Maca, Yura), Yura health clinic, Bosque de Queñua reforestation.
  - Component 3: Transversal Support Activities - Institutional Strengthening (US$3.46M) - marketing/branding plan, tourist web platform, capacity building, M&E observatory, rapid tourist assistance system.
  - Component 4: Project Implementation Unit (US$5.91M) - administrative, fiduciary, and E&S execution functions.
- Delivery Model: Investment Project Financing (IPF) with IBRD loan to Republic of Peru (MEF), implemented by GORE Arequipa via a newly created PIU, with MINCETUR offering technical oversight and counterpart funds.
- Timeline: Approval projected July 2026; Closing June 30, 2032.
- Budget: Total US$97.80M (IBRD: US$77.20M, Counterpart: US$20.60M).
- Key Stakeholders: MEF, MINCETUR, GORE Arequipa, Ministry of Culture, MTC, Ministry of Housing, Ministry of Health, SERNANP, local municipalities (Sibayo, Yanque, Yura, San Juan de Tarucani, Maca), local/indigenous communities, private sector.
- External Dependencies: Interinstitutional agreements with participating municipalities, cooperation agreement between MINCETUR and GORE Arequipa, counterpart funding availability.

Step 2 - Category sweep
- technical: High road traffic fatality rate and poor tertiary road condition in Arequipa; lack of ongoing O&M arrangements threatening asset sustainability post-completion.
- financial: Budget allocation and execution delays within the Peruvian public financial framework; financial reporting inaccuracies due to lack of WB experience.
- schedule: Delay in executing required Interinstitutional Agreements before Component 1 & 2 disbursements; delays in staffing key PIU roles post-effectiveness.
- stakeholder: Exposure to Sexual Exploitation and Abuse / Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) in project areas hindering female workforce participation; difficulties in M&E tracking due to high informality in local employment.
- political_regulatory: Highly fragmented institutional landscape across line ministries and subnational governments affecting project coordination and budgeting.
- environmental: Vulnerability to climate hazards (flooding, landslides, heavy rains, seismic activity) damaging roads, water networks, viewpoints, and historic heritage sites.
- organizational: PIU lack of experience with World Bank/multilateral operations leading to procurement and implementation delays; unclear internal PIU roles and control procedures.
- external: Market volatility and macroeconomic shocks impacting tourist arrival growth, length of stay, and spending projections.

Step 3 - Evidence filter
All identified risks are directly grounded in explicit text statements within the Project Appraisal Document (sections on Key Risks, Appraisal Summary, Fiduciary, Environmental/Social, and Sectoral Context).

Step 4 - Assess
Assign likelihood (1-5), impact (1-5), concrete mitigations, and exact quotes (<=25 words) for each surviving risk.

Step 5 - Consolidate
Consolidate into 13 well-supported, distinct risks spanning all categories without duplicate overlap.

risks.description: PIU's lack of experience with World Bank policies and procedures may lead to implementation bottlenecks, procurement delays, and non-compliance with World Bank standards.
risks.mitigation: Implement targeted capacity building and training programs supported by the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) and hire experienced technical specialists.
risks.evidence: Given the lack of experience of the PIU with World Bank or other multilateral-financed projects, targeted capacity building and training... will be required.

risks.description: Initial budget allocation and execution delays within the national public financial system may disrupt project readiness and disbursement rates.
risks.mitigation: GORE Arequipa will initiate budget allocation processes for external and local resources immediately upon loan signing as detailed in the POM.
risks.evidence: In Peru, initial project implementation phases often experience delays in budget allocation and low budget execution rates, which could affect project readiness...

risks.description: Institutional fragmentation across multiple line ministries and subnational entities could impede cross-sectoral coordination and project implementation.
risks.mitigation: Establish a high-level Steering Committee (Comité Directivo) and Consultative Committee (Comité Consultivo) to facilitate inter-institutional alignment and issue resolution.
risks.evidence: Efficient budgeting and implementation of investments in tourism are hindered by lack of coordination within a highly fragmented institutional landscape...

risks.description: Climate-induced natural hazards such as heavy rains, flooding, landslides, and seismic events could cause severe physical damage to roads, tourist facilities, and cultural heritage sites.
risks.mitigation: Incorporate climate-resilient engineering standards, improved drainage systems, slope stabilization, structural reinforcement, and rapid tourist assistance systems into project designs.
risks.evidence: The main climate and natural hazard risks to the operation include heavy rains, flooding, and landslides, in addition to high seismic activity.

risks.description: Delays in executing required Interinstitutional Agreements with participating municipalities and stakeholders could halt disbursements and civil works for Components 1 and 2.
risks.mitigation: Prioritize early drafting, negotiation, and signing of interinstitutional agreements with target municipalities prior to initiating procurement.
risks.evidence: No withdrawals shall be made for Goods, works... for Parts/components 1 and 2... until and unless the Bank has received at least three signed Interinstitutional Agreements...

risks.description: Poor baseline condition of the tertiary rural road network and high regional traffic fatality rates could compromise tourist safety and access to key corridor attractions.
risks.mitigation: Integrate dedicated road safety features (signage, guardrails, speed calming) and structural upgrades into all tertiary road rehabilitation technical designs.
risks.evidence: In 2024, Arequipa recorded 11.7 road traffic deaths per 100,000 people... 82 percent of the red vecinal is in poor condition.

risks.description: Inadequate operation and maintenance (O&M) arrangements following civil works completion could result in rapid deterioration of constructed water, sanitation, and transport assets.
risks.mitigation: Establish clear municipal O&M agreements, operational management manuals, and capacity building for local utilities and asset managers prior to asset handover.
risks.evidence: ...the project will support arrangements that ensure mechanisms are in place for the ongoing maintenance and sustainability of the improved assets.

risks.description: Risks related to Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA) and Sexual Harassment (SH) during construction and tourism operations could harm local communities and restrict female participation.
risks.mitigation: Formulate and implement a comprehensive SEA/SH Action Plan within 120 days of effectiveness, alongside codes of conduct and worker training.
risks.evidence: Contributors to the gender gap include... exposure to sexual harassment and exploitation risks...

risks.description: Accounting errors and inaccurate financial reporting may occur due to the PIU's unfamiliarity with World Bank financial management requirements.
risks.mitigation: Utilize the national SIAF system supplemented by specialized Bank FM guidelines, POM internal control procedures, and annual independent external audits.
risks.evidence: Inadequate experience with Bank-financed projects may result in errors in financial records and reporting.

risks.description: Vulnerability of tourism projections to broader macroeconomic shocks or demand volatility could lead to lower tourist arrivals and reduced economic returns.
risks.mitigation: Execute targeted multi-market promotional campaigns (Component 3) and diversify market segments across adventure, cultural, and domestic eco-tourism.
risks.evidence: A sensitivity analysis was conducted to assess the robustness of the model by applying economic shocks to the main variables...

risks.description: Unclear internal organizational roles, responsibilities, and key controls within the newly created PIU could lead to administrative delays and operational inefficiencies.
risks.mitigation: Define explicit operational workflows, reporting channels, key staff functions, and control mechanisms within the Project Operational Manual (POM).
risks.evidence: Unclear internal coordination and roles within the PIU... POM will include the definition of clear roles and responsibilities...

risks.description: Structural challenges in measuring localized informal sector employment could hinder accurate monitoring and evaluation of project job creation impacts.
risks.mitigation: Deploy advanced M&E remote sensing methodologies, satellite imagery, AI algorithms, and disaggregated household surveys (ENAHO) to track formal and informal employment gains.
risks.evidence: Measuring the impact of project interventions on jobs is difficult considering the high level of informality, the lack of monitoring of jobs...

risks.description: Delays in the timely recruitment and appointment of key PIU technical, legal, and environmental/social staff post-effectiveness could delay overall implementation.
risks.mitigation: Enforce the legal covenant mandating the appointment of key PIU personnel (technical, legal, E&S, infrastructure heads) no later than 60 days after Effectiveness.
risks.evidence: Delayed recruitment of FM staff. To manage this risk, terms of reference for all the FM positions... shall be appointed within two months after effectiveness.
